title: Singleton arena never resolves on pointer-down; first slop-crossing move is dropped under DragStartBehavior.start
evidence: sample_list_fling (six 40 px moves): Flutter offset 40 at 48 ms, Incular 0; every later offset 40 px behind; settled 1193.7479 vs 1153.7479. Same mechanism in other twins: gestures__dismissible_threshold (one 100 px move; Incular progress stays 0 and onDismissed never fires; Flutter progress 0.625 at 48 ms and dismisses at 1032 ms); gestures__draggable_drop_target (Flutter onDragStarted at 32 ms, before any move; Incular at 48 ms after the move; accepted data identical at 80 ms). See also gestures-004.
impact: Every scroll, swipe-to-dismiss and draggable drag starts one slop (18 px touch, 36 px pan) late, and the slop-crossing delta is discarded. Dismissible thresholds and scroll positions are offset by that amount.
cause: Flutter closes the arena after pointer-down and a closed arena with one member picks it (arena.dart:251-276). Incular widget arenas have no close or sole-member default (external resolver path in arena_member.rs); the recognizer accepts on the threshold-crossing move and DragStartBehavior.start drops that delta (pointer.rs:635-665). The close helper in arena_member.rs:120 is used only standalone.
fix_direction: Resolve a sole-member arena on pointer-down, as Flutter closes the arena after the press. Keep competition when several members joined. Recheck scroll, scale, dismissible and draggable starts afterwards.
limitations: Verified at HEAD on sample_list_fling and the dismissible and draggable twins. Source mechanism read, not instrumented.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Double-tap-only GestureDetector never fires onDoubleTap
evidence: Frame 0 and frame count match (9 frames). Flutter count 1 from 80 ms; Incular stays 0 through the end. Scene sets onDoubleTap without onTap.
impact: A GestureDetector with only onDoubleTap silently never fires.
cause: Flutter tracks the first tap in a dedicated DoubleTapGestureRecognizer. Incular records last_tap only in the regular tap-up branch (pointer.rs:763-782), which runs only when onTap, onTapUp or onTapCancel exist, so the first up is rejected with no first-tap state.
fix_direction: Track the first tap independently of onTap callbacks, as the separate Flutter recognizer does.
limitations: Checked with onDoubleTap alone; onTap plus onDoubleTap combinations were not run.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: onLongPress fires on release instead of at the 500 ms deadline
evidence: onLongPressStart position matches (start_y 300 at 528 ms). onLongPress count is 1 in Flutter at 528 ms and 0 in Incular until pointer-up.
impact: onLongPress is delayed to release while the pointer is held; a held-press action runs only when the finger lifts, or not at all if the gesture is cancelled.
cause: Incular poll() returns only LongPressStart at the deadline (pointer.rs:291-312); the LongPress action is emitted in the pointer-up branch (pointer.rs:700-738) and dispatched from there (pointer.rs:818-827).
fix_direction: Dispatch onLongPress with onLongPressStart at the deadline; keep onLongPressEnd at release.
limitations: Only the 500 ms hold with no movement was run.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Scale start and pinch values wait for the arena, so single-pointer start is late and two-pointer span is measured late
evidence: Single pointer: Flutter starts at 32 ms (before the first move), Incular at 48 ms after the first move; focal y matches afterwards. Pinch (gestures__scale__two_pointer_pinch): both contacts delivered; pointer count 2 at 48 ms in Flutter, 64 ms in Incular. Flutter scale 1.5 at 48 ms and 1.8333 at 64 ms; Incular reports 1.0 at every frame through 96 ms because its initial span is taken at late acceptance (scale.rs:368).
impact: Scale onStart fires one move late; pinch scale is wrong for the whole gesture (final scale 1.0 instead of 1.83 in the scene).
cause: Same missing sole-member resolution as gestures-001 for the scale member. Incular scale waits for focal movement past slop; the initial span is measured at acceptance rather than when the contacts start.
fix_direction: Share the gestures-001 arena fix with scale. Measure the initial span from the contacts when the scale starts, not from the acceptance frame.
limitations: Two-pointer case only for the scene order used (second down, move, first move, second up).
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: LongPressDraggable converts to an immediate Draggable and ignores the long-press delay
evidence: Down at 16 ms, 40 px move at 116 ms (before the 500 ms delay). Flutter never starts a drag. Incular starts a drag at 132 ms and reports it active until release. Both twins now record an active flag (Flutter onDragStarted to onDragEnd), so the value is equivalent.
impact: A quick swipe on a LongPressDraggable drags immediately, which conflicts with a surrounding scroll or swipe and cannot be deferred.
cause: LongPressDraggable::from builds a plain Draggable (drag_drop.rs:599) with no delay, no long-press recognizer and no onStart. Feedback and delay options are absent from the type.
fix_direction: Carry a delayed-start mode through the drag source (kLongPressTimeout, DelayedMultiDragGestureRecognizer semantics) and give LongPressDraggable feedback and callback parameters.
limitations: Divergence verified for a move before the deadline only; the long-hold path (drag starting at 500 ms) was not run.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: ReorderableDelayedDragStartListener never starts a reorder when the long-press deadline fires on a frame tick
evidence: Timeline (both twins): mount at 0 ms; frame at 16 ms; touch down at 16 ms on row 0; pump 600 ms (frame at 616 ms; the 500 ms deadline falls inside the pump); move 150 px down at 616 ms; two frames; up. Flutter: started_index 0 at 616 ms, row 0 at y 150 at 632 ms, row 1 slides up, ended_index 2 at 664 ms. Incular: started_index stays -1 for the whole run, row 0 never leaves its slot, ended_index never fires. Twin check: both use a 500 ms delay (Flutter default kLongPressTimeout; Incular LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT through on_long_press_start), a touch pointer on both (Flutter TestGesture touch; Incular touch input), identical 16 ms frames on the fake clock, identical rows and 600 ms hold. The existing unit test crates/incular-widgets/tests/reorderable.rs delayed_listener_rejects_early_motion_and_starts_after_long_press passes; it fires the deadline on a Move event with no frame pump, and the timer-driven path does not start the drag.
impact: The delayed reorder pattern used on touch lists (long press on an item, then drag) does not reorder in a running app, where frames fire the deadline before the first move. This is the common mobile path.
cause: Hypothesis, not instrumented: the delayed listener is a long-press GestureDetector wrapping the Draggable. The Draggable immediate recognizer joins the arena with simultaneous false (interaction.rs:702). When pump_gesture_timers accepts the long press on a frame (interaction.rs:1366-1372), apply_arena_entries rejects the pending Draggable member, so the later move has no drag recognizer. The move-driven deadline in the unit test orders these differently and still passes.
fix_direction: Make the delayed listener one delayed drag recognizer (Flutter DelayedMultiDragGestureRecognizer semantics) rather than a long-press detector around an immediate drag. Add a frame-driven reorder case to the Incular unit tests.
confidence: high for the observed failure; medium for the arena mechanism
limitations: Mechanism inferred from source and the passing unit test; not isolated with a debugger. The onReorder index convention was not compared because no reorder completes.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: GestureDetector has no secondary or tertiary tap or long-press callbacks
evidence: rg for secondary, tertiary and right-click in crates/incular-gestures/src and crates/incular-widgets/src/gestures.rs finds nothing. Flutter GestureDetector exposes 4 secondary tap, 4 secondary long-press, 3 tertiary tap and 7 tertiary long-press callbacks. Incular recognizers accept only the primary button (default allowed_buttons filter in multidrag.rs and tap_and_drag.rs).
impact: Right-click and middle-click actions (context menus, middle-button handling) cannot be attached to a GestureDetector; right-click does nothing.
cause: Recognizers accept only the primary button by design. No secondary or tertiary recognizer exists.
fix_direction: Add secondary and tertiary tap and long-press recognizers (or button-filtered variants) and expose the Flutter callback set on GestureDetector.
limitations: Source only. FrameHarness sends touch and mouse-wheel input, so a right-click twin cannot be built yet (harness request).
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md
verification_note: Verification: right-click context menus exist in incular-controls (context_menu Trigger); the gap is the neutral GestureDetector callbacks.

title: GestureDetector lacks onTapMove, onLongPressDown, onLongPressCancel and force-press callbacks; the force-press recognizer is unwired
evidence: Builders present in gestures.rs: tap, tap_down, tap_up, tap_cancel, double_tap, double_tap_down, double_tap_cancel, long_press, long_press_start, long_press_move_update, long_press_up, long_press_end, pan, horizontal and vertical drags, scale, trackpad, cancel. Missing: onTapMove, onLongPressDown, onLongPressCancel, all onForcePress*. ForcePressGestureRecognizer exists (force_press.rs:44) but nothing constructs it in the widget layer.
impact: Apps cannot respond to press-down before the long-press deadline, to long-press cancellation, to drag-within-tap, or to pressure gestures through GestureDetector.
cause: Callbacks were not wired from recognizers to the widget API; force press was ported in the gestures crate only.
fix_direction: Wire onLongPressDown and onLongPressCancel from the existing long-press state, add onTapMove from tap-move state, and construct ForcePressGestureRecognizer from GestureDetector callbacks.
limitations: Source only. Force input is not available in FrameHarness.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Draggable feedback is never painted by the framework
flutter_ref: widgets/drag_target.dart (_DragAvatar: feedback placed in an Overlay entry, _build)
evidence: The feedback builder is stored and a snapshot is exposed through DragDropContext::feedback(). rg for feedback() in crates and examples finds no consumer, so no widget paints the dragged preview. The scenario does not record the preview (the recorder does not probe it), so the difference is source-only.
impact: Dragging shows no preview unless the application reads DragDropContext::feedback() and paints it. Feedback offset, DragBoundary clamping (drag_boundary.rs) and feedbackOffset therefore have no visible effect by default.
cause: The design keeps drag feedback out of the navigation-independent crate and expects the app to present it through its own Overlay (documented at drag_drop.rs:1-8). Flutter presents it automatically.
fix_direction: Provide a default overlay presentation of the feedback (or an opt-in helper) so Draggable matches Flutter by default; keep the snapshot API.
limitations: Design intent is documented; the default visible difference is the finding. The pixel harness could confirm it; not run.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: DragTarget that rejects a candidate gets no onLeave or onMove, and nested targets do not fall through
flutter_ref: widgets/drag_target.dart:776-790 (didLeave for every entered target), :803-806 (didMove), :905-947 (updateDrag enters the first accepting target in path order), :950-958 (_getDragTargets returns all targets in the path)
incular_ref: crates/incular-widgets/src/tree/interaction.rs:1785-1795 (drag_target_ancestor returns the nearest target only), :1796-1830 (update_drag_target); crates/incular-widgets/src/drag_drop.rs:519-530 (enter returns false before storing the target)
evidence: Flutter keeps rejected targets in _enteredTargets, so onMove and onLeave fire for them, and the search continues to outer targets. Incular enter() returns false without storing the target, so leave() and update() are skipped for rejecting targets, and drag_target_ancestor takes only the nearest DragTarget, so an outer accepting target never receives the drop.
impact: Apps that show hover state from onLeave or onMove see nothing for a target that rejects the payload. Nested drop zones where the inner rejects lose the drop entirely.
cause: Single-target model: enter() decides once per hit, and target lookup stops at the first DragTarget ancestor.
fix_direction: Track every hit DragTarget as entered, call onMove for each, call onLeave for each on exit, and try outer targets in path order when an inner target rejects.
limitations: Source only. Not scenario-tested; a nested-target twin needs a second DragTarget in the Flutter scene, which the current scenes do not build.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: DragTarget has no builder with candidate and rejected data
evidence: DragTarget::new takes a child widget only; no builder receives candidate or rejected payloads.
impact: Hover highlight depends on application state set from on_enter and on_leave, which the Flutter builder pattern avoids.
cause: Target rendering is static; candidate state is not exposed to the build.
fix_direction: Add a builder variant that receives candidate and rejected payload lists and rebuilds when they change.
limitations: API-shape difference; no runtime failure claimed. Depends partly on gestures-010.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Dismissible fling slides out over a fixed movement duration instead of Flutter fling simulation
incular_ref: crates/incular-widgets/src/dismissible.rs:1-20 (documented in Dismissible docs); :334-360 (drag_end fling branch); MOVEMENT_DURATION 200 ms
evidence: The Incular Dismissible docs state that a fling slides out over the remaining movement_duration rather than Flutter spring simulation. Flutter calls AnimationController.fling with the release velocity, which uses a spring simulation.
impact: Fling dismissals move on a different curve and length than Flutter; thresholds and final position match, the motion does not.
cause: Deliberate simplification documented in the widget.
fix_direction: Use the same spring simulation as AnimationController.fling for the fling branch.
limitations: Documented deviation; the simulation difference was read, not measured. No fling twin in the scenario set.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: InteractiveViewer lacks trackpadScrollCausesScale; DeviceGestureSettings slop overrides absent
evidence: rg for trackpad_scroll_causes_scale and DeviceGestureSettings finds nothing. Flutter default trackpadScrollCausesScale is false, so default behavior matches; the opt-in path and platform slop overrides are absent.
impact: Apps cannot opt trackpad scrolling into zoom, and platform touch or pan slop overrides from MediaQuery gestureSettings are ignored.
fix_direction: Port trackpadScrollCausesScale with kDefaultTrackpadScrollToScaleFactor; add a settings input to slop computation.
limitations: Default behavior unaffected. Trackpad input not in harness.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: DiagonalDragBehavior lacks Flutter's weightedEvent/weightedContinuous distinction
evidence: Flutter has four values: weightedEvent locks the axis once per drag, weightedContinuous re-evaluates it on every update. Incular has a single Weighted value.
impact: Two-dimensional scroll views cannot reproduce one of Flutter's two weighted diagonal-drag behaviors; which one Weighted matches was not established.
cause: The two weighted modes were merged.
fix_direction: Split Weighted into the two Flutter modes and document the default.
limitations: Source only; behavior of Incular's Weighted was not compared with either Flutter mode.
